question: Does `temperature` reach the GLM sampler?
control: generate.py calls torch.manual_seed(self.seed) at the top of every generate(), so two calls on ONE loaded model share an identical RNG stream and differ only in temperature.

setup.env: HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 (the Hub re-fetch path segfaults intermittently on this host)

after_fix.direction_check: lower T -> sharper -> higher GC (0.547); higher T -> flatter -> GC toward uniform 0.5 (0.497). Mechanistically correct ordering, not merely 'the numbers moved'.

mechanism.remote_processor: _BPLogitsProcessor marginalises k-mer logits to per-base probs, samples, and returns a ONE-HOT (-inf everywhere, 0.0 at the selected token)
mechanism.hf_ordering: transformers 5.14.1 generation/utils.py: user processors merged at line 1257, TemperatureLogitsWarper appended at line 1276 -- i.e. AFTER
mechanism.arithmetic: temperature on a one-hot is identity (0/T==0, -inf/T==-inf)
mechanism.upstream_docstring_is_inverted: it claims the processor 'Runs LAST ... so that temperature / top-k / top-p etc. influence the marginal distributions before base selection'
mechanism.sampling_was_never_broken: sequences within a single call always differed; only the knobs were dead

fix: HFGenerator._sampling_processors() passes TemperatureLogitsWarper / TopKLogitsWarper via logits_processor=, which the remote generate places BEFORE its bp processor (`existing + [bp_proc]`); the inert temperature=/top_k= kwargs are no longer passed. No remote code or model-cache file is modified.
non_vacuity: reverting to the pre-fix file fails 4 of 6 tests incl. the regression pin; all 6 pass after
does_not_invalidate: the sweep's 0.8141 distinguishability, which is a valid measurement of DEFAULT sampling
does_invalidate: any GLM artifact dated <= 2026-10-19 whose `sampling` block records a non-1.0 temperature or non-zero top_k -- every such run used default sampling regardless
reopens: whether temperature/top_k move distinguishability was NEVER tested, because the knob was inert. Open and cheap (~90 s). NOT claimed here that they will help.
